title: Excess intergalactic heating around a dual quasar system 2.8 Gyr after the Big Bang - Nature Astronomy
byline: Hall; Kirsten R; Zakamska; Nadia L; Bennett; Jake S; Chen; Yu-Ching; Fan; Xiaohui
html:
Abstract

Galaxy formation models necessitate that actively growing supermassive black holes, or quasars, strongly impact their environments. Theory suggests that quasar winds produce very hot gas bubbles that extend through the host galaxy and into the circumgalactic medium. Because this gas component is so hot and diffuse, the only way to measure its total energy is through the thermal Sunyaev–Zel’dovich effect. Here we report the discovery of a dual quasar system at z = 2.37, which is embedded in a bubble of hot gas as detected (at 6σ) by a thermal Sunyaev–Zel’dovich flux decrement at millimetre wavelengths. The total thermal energy of the hot gas is 9.7 × 1060 erg. This energy exceeds the amount expected from all of the hot gas in a 1013 M⊙ dark matter halo by a factor of 3.6, and constitutes at least 0.6% of the quasar’s lifetime energy output. We also find evidence for hot gas on larger (100–600 kpc) scales that may also originate in quasar outflows. This considerable excess energy is more than sufficient to shut off star formation and heat the intergalactic medium, implying a significant impact from quasar-driven winds on their surroundings. Such feedback plausibly explains the steep decline of the bright end of the luminosity function of galaxies across the observable Universe.

Data availability

All data used in this publication are publicly available via National Radio Astronomy Observatory (NRAO) archives and the Submillimeter Array Radio Telescope Data Center. This research makes use of ALMA data (project IDs: 2018.1.01806.S, 2019.1.01070.S and 2024.1.00933.S) and VLA data (project IDs: 19A-160, 20A-323, 20A-363, 22A-253 and 23A-076), which can be accessed via the NRAO’s science-ready data products portal at https://data.nrao.edu/. This research makes use of the Submillimeter Array Project 2020A-S051, which is available via the public data archive at https://lweb.cfa.harvard.edu/sma-archive/. This research has made use of the VLASS primary beam-corrected images VLASS-QL_1.2_J154938+124500, VLASS-QL_2.2_J154938+124500 and VLASS-QL_3.2_J154938+124500, which can be obtained at https://cutouts.cirada.ca, operated by the Canadian Initiative for Radio Astronomy Data Analysis (CIRADA). This research has made use of the FIRST (Faint Images of the Radio Sky at Twenty-cm) survey cutout image centred on J1549+1245, which can be found by entering the RA and Dec at https://sundog.stsci.edu/cgi-bin/firstcutout.
